title: Du Moulin the son: fiducia of refuge justifies — fiducia of sense follows
source_text: LI. Horum autem vestigia sequitur Pet. Molinaeus, Petri Molinaei filius, jam supra nominatus. Nam tractatu supra citato, de forma, sive natura fidei justificantis, duplicem quoque fiduciam distinguit. Prior est per quam ad Deum confugimus, & ipsi innitimur, de qua dicitur apud Psaltem, In te Domine confido, non confundar in aeternum, Psalm. 31. & apud Isaiam, cap. 50. Confidat in nomine Domini, & innitatur super Deum suum. Posterior est qua, Spiritu Dei contestante Spiritui nostro, confidimus Deum nobis esse in Jesu Christo reconciliatum, & vitam aeternam ad nos pertinere; unde nascitur pax conscientiae, & sancta quaedam securitas. Quae posterior fiducia ex priori nascitur, juxta illud Apostoli, In quo habemus fiduciam & accessum in confidentia per fidem ejus, Ephes. 3. 12. Priorem fiduciam vocat fiduciam perfugii, posteriorem fiduciam sensus. Quibus positis affirmat, non fiduciam sensus, sed solam fiduciam perfugii, sive motum illum conscientiae, quae reatus sui conscia Dei per Christum misericordiam amplectitur atque apprehendit, esse instrumentum justificationis nostrae, & formam essentialem fidei justificantis. Idque quoniam Dei promissiones factae sunt illis qui ad Christum veniunt, & justitiam ac Dei gratiam in Christo quaerunt atque esuriunt, non vero illis qui jam Christum possident, & compotes gratiae facti sunt. Ac praeterea quoniam fiducia illa sensus, justificationem jam factam praesupponit; ac proinde non potest esse illius causa, aut instrumentum. Et postea observat duplicem esse in fide actionem: unam directam, per quam Christum amplectimur, eique adhaeremus; alteram vero reflexam per quam actionem illam nostram recognoscimus, & sentimus nos Christum apprehendisse; ex quo sensu posterior fiducia nascitur. Et per priorem actum nos proprie credere in Christum, & justificari, non vero per posteriorem. Adeoque multos esse qui Christum vere apprehendunt, nec dum tamen sentiunt se illum apprehendisse; qui nihilominus coram Deo vere justificati sunt, etsi de eo nondum certi & persuasi sint; quoniam haec persuasio non pertinet ad fidei essentiam, sed solum ad ejus perfectionem, & est verae ac robustae fidei fructus, ac consequens quoddam.
pass_a_gloss: But their footsteps Peter du Moulin, son of Peter du Moulin, already named above, follows. For in the treatise cited above on the form or nature of justifying faith he also distinguishes a twofold trust. The former is that by which we flee to God and lean on Him, of which it is said in the Psalmist, In Thee, O Lord, I trust; let me never be confounded, Psalm 31; and in Isaiah chapter 50, Let him trust in the name of the Lord, and lean upon his God. The latter is that by which, the Spirit of God bearing witness with our spirit, we trust that God is reconciled to us in Jesus Christ, and that eternal life pertains to us; whence arises peace of conscience and a certain holy security. Which latter trust is born from the former, according to that of the Apostle, In whom we have trust and access with confidence by His faith, Ephesians 3:12. The former trust he calls trust of refuge, the latter trust of sense. Which being laid down, he affirms that not the trust of sense, but only the trust of refuge — or that motion of conscience which, conscious of its guilt, embraces and apprehends God's mercy through Christ — is the instrument of our justification and the essential form of justifying faith. And that because God's promises are made to those who come to Christ and seek and hunger for justice and God's grace in Christ, not to those who already possess Christ and have been made partakers of grace. And besides because that trust of sense presupposes justification already made; and therefore cannot be its cause or instrument. And afterward he observes that there is a twofold action in faith: one direct, by which we embrace Christ and adhere to Him; but the other reflex, by which we recognize that action of ours and feel that we have apprehended Christ; from which sense the latter trust is born. And by the former act we properly believe in Christ and are justified, not by the latter. And so there are many who truly apprehend Christ and yet do not yet feel that they have apprehended Him; who nevertheless are truly justified before God, even if they are not yet sure and persuaded of it; because this persuasion does not pertain to the essence of faith, but only to its perfection, and is a fruit and certain consequent of true and robust faith.
pass_b_english: Pierre du Moulin the son: twofold fiducia.
Fiducia of refuge — flee to God / lean on Him (Ps 31; Isa 50) — instrument and essential form.
Fiducia of sense — Spirit-witness that God is reconciled and life is ours — born from the former (Eph 3:12).
Promises belong to those coming hungry to Christ, not to those who already possess Him.
Sense-fiducia presupposes justification — cannot cause it.
Direct act justifies; reflex sense may lag — many justified without yet feeling they have Christ.
